The evidence of the current information given to patients at 40 weeks' pregnant on the decision over whether to accept the offer of an induction from 41 weeks does not reflect NICE guidance on the information needed by patients to make an informed choice on induction. Whilst it provides details of the risks associated with induction, it does not provide information on the risks of continuing with pregnancy beyond 41 weeks.
inadequate patient information on induction risks

The evidence given at inquest indicated a lack of understanding and/or consistency over when concerns about labouring mothers and/or the CTG trace should be escalated for doctor review. Evidence was given on the measures put in place to address issues with escalation, including
there was no liaison between Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow and UCLH as to the plan for the delivery of the baby
lack of coordinated delivery plan between tertiary hospitals and Princess Alexandra Hospital
there needs to be a review of the system that exists between the tertiary hospitals and Princess Alexandra Hospital as to how to formulate an Agreed Delivery Plan for both mother and baby
absence of agreed delivery plan for mother and baby
